solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Twits we maltreated in quarrel? It's difficult to say

indicators.note: the reworked letters sit inside the word for a quarrel

parts.note: a jar is a jarring dispute or quarrel

indicators.note: words that have been maltreated are knocked about and come out in a different order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone mistreats a pair of fools during a row, and the result is hard to put into words.
explanation.walkthrough: JAR opens to take the rearranged letters: JA + WTWISTE + R gives JAW-TWISTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A jaw-twister is a word or phrase so awkward to pronounce that it seems to contort the mouth.

clue.text: Concerning estate owned outright, a look on face says it all!

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece placed on another is written above it, so it comes first

parts.note: taken as written
lo is an old exclamation meaning look or behold
dial is slang for a person's face

explanation.surface: One knowing glance tells you everything you need to know.
explanation.walkthrough: A + LO + DIAL. Allodial land is held absolutely, owing no rent or service to any overlord.
explanation.definitionFit: Allodial (also alodial) is the legal adjective for land held in absolute ownership, the opposite of feudal tenure.

clue.text: United involved in contest defeat Celtic

indicators.note: a thing involved in something is wrapped up within it

parts.note: a war is a contest between sides
U is the standard abbreviation for United in team names

explanation.surface: A football report: United, in a tussle, beat Celtic, the Glasgow club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Celtic' looks like the beaten Glasgow team; it is the flag that the answer is a Scots word. WA(U)R.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots, waur is both the comparative 'worse' and a verb meaning to worst or overcome an opponent.

clue.text: Part-exchange, 50% of deal going into process

indicators.note: the kept letters go into the other word, sitting inside it

parts.note: a train is a sequence of events, a process

indicators.note: half of a four-letter word means keeping just its opening pair

parts.note: the first half of the word

explanation.surface: Half a car deal gets swallowed up by the bureaucratic process.
explanation.walkthrough: TRA(DE)IN. A trade-in is the old item handed over as part payment.
explanation.definitionFit: Part-exchange is the British term for handing in an old item as partial payment, which Americans call a trade-in.

clue.text: Wife must have e.g. Aga, getting spliced?

indicators.note: one piece must have the other alongside it, so they join end to end

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for wife
an Aga is a well-known make of British range cooker

explanation.surface: A wife insists on an Aga stove as a condition of getting married.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spliced' looks like slang for married, fitting the wife; here it is the weaving sense. An Aga is a heavy British kitchen range.
explanation.definitionFit: Splicing joins rope strands by interweaving them, so something spliced has been woven together.

clue.text: Exchange old recipe used in cheap stew, special part of meal

indicators.note: the abbreviation is used inside the dish, placed within it

parts.note: scouse is a Liverpool stew of cheap meat and vegetables
R is the abbreviation for recipe on prescriptions

explanation.surface: An old recipe goes into a cheap stew that is a special part of the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: SCO(R)USE; the end of the clue is a second route, S (special) + COURSE (part of meal). Scourse is an old word for exchange or barter.
explanation.definitionFit: Scourse is an obsolete word for trading or bartering, so it means exchange in an old sense.

clue.text: No longer relished receiving ball — like one treated to bumper?

indicators.note: a word receiving something takes it in, holding it inside

parts.note: relished in the past tense, something once savoured
a ball is round, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: A cricketer no longer enjoys facing the ball after being hit by a bouncer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bumper' suggests a cricket bouncer; it is a brimming glass raised in a toast. T(O)ASTED.
explanation.definitionFit: A bumper is a glass filled to the brim for drinking a health, so someone honoured with one has been toasted.

clue.text: One in grip of retro, going wild?

definitions.text: One in grip of retro, going wild?

indicators.note: a thing in the grip of another is held inside it
letters going wild run riot and lose their order

parts.note: taken as written, to be jumbled
the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone caught up in nostalgia goes wild.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a rioter is one who goes wild, and the wordplay is I in a wild version of RETRO.
explanation.definitionFit: A rioter is someone taking part in a violent public disturbance, a person running amok.

clue.text: I am attached to pagan deity — or was

indicators.note: one piece attached to another is tacked on after it

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of shepherds and the wild
the contraction I'm

explanation.surface: Someone declares devotion to a heathen god, perhaps only in the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pagan deity' reads as one phrase meaning Pan; the definition is 'pagan' alone, with 'or was' marking an obsolete word.
explanation.definitionFit: Panim is an archaic form of paynim, an old word for a heathen or non-Christian, especially a Muslim.

clue.text: Reworked epics that'll include new limerick typically?

indicators.note: the words will include another letter, taking it in among them
something reworked is remade, its letters put in fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Revised epic poems will now feature a limerick.
explanation.walkthrough: The extra N joins the letters of EPICS THAT before they are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentastich is a poem or stanza of five lines, and a limerick is the best-known five-line form.

clue.text: What'll start cancer of the mouth returning? A cigar

indicators.note: what will start a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter

indicators.note: a word returning goes back the way it came, read from right to left

parts.note: oral means relating to the mouth

explanation.surface: A grim health warning: a cigar is what will bring on mouth cancer.
explanation.walkthrough: C + LARO.
explanation.definitionFit: A claro is a light-coloured, mild cigar, the name coming from Spanish for light or clear.

clue.text: Coal fires may generate small fluid bits of slag like this

indicators.note: rearranged, the letters may generate two new strings

parts.note: taken as written
fl is the short form of fluid, as in fl oz; these letters are taken away

explanation.surface: Burning coal leaves behind small runny fragments of slag.
explanation.walkthrough: A compositional clue: the letters of COAL FIRES rearrange into FL plus the answer, 'like this' saying the answer is what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Scoriae are the clinker-like fragments of slag or porous volcanic rock; the word is the plural of scoria.

clue.text: Her embroidered jacket girl displayed — see gold lining from rear

indicators.note: a lining sits within something, so these letters go inside the name

parts.note: a girl's name

indicators.note: read from the rear means read from its end back to its start

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
v is the abbreviation for vide, Latin for see

explanation.surface: A girl shows off her embroidered jacket, with gold thread lining visible at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: ZO(UAV)E. 'Her' marks this as a woman's garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A zouave is a short, open, often embroidered jacket for women, modelled on the uniform of French Algerian infantry.

clue.text: Customs union

parts.note: read plainly: an agreement between states abolishing internal tariffs
the setter's intent: this was Azed's competition entry, given a bare definition for solvers to write their own clue

explanation.walkthrough: Azed's monthly competition puzzle leaves one answer with just a definition; solvers send in their own clue for it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Zollverein was the nineteenth-century German customs union that removed tariffs between member states.

clue.text: Pilot opposed to diminution of navy

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
N is the abbreviation for navy, the word shrunk to one letter

explanation.surface: A pilot is against cutting back the navy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pilot' looks like a person; it is a verb, to steer. CON + N.
explanation.definitionFit: To conn a ship is to direct its steering, which is what a pilot does when guiding a vessel.

clue.text: My nest is large (depending) though it's quiet inside

indicators.note: one word goes inside another, splitting it

parts.note: but and though both introduce a contrast
sh is the call for quiet
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of a large nest, though it's peaceful within.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the bird speaking: a bushtit builds a big hanging (depending) nest. BU(SH)T + IT.
explanation.definitionFit: The bushtit is a tiny North American songbird famous for weaving a large, pendulous sock-shaped nest.

clue.text: 51 and old-looking? Able to get away — a good chap at a party

definitions.text: a good chap at a party

parts.note: LI is 51 in Roman numerals

indicators.note: a word able to get away leaves, so it is removed from the longer one

parts.note: venerable means aged and dignified
taken as written; these letters go

explanation.surface: A fifty-one-year-old who looks older but can still make a getaway livens up a party.
explanation.walkthrough: LI + VENER(able).
explanation.definitionFit: A livener is someone or something that livens things up, the sort of guest every party needs.

clue.text: A dash of milk in tea? That's the idea

indicators.note: the letter goes in the other word

parts.note: Thea is the old botanical genus name of the tea plant

indicators.note: a dash is a tiny amount, here just the opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter

explanation.surface: A splash of milk in your tea: that's the way to do it.
explanation.walkthrough: THE(M)A. Thea as tea is a Chambers word that Azed solvers know.
explanation.definitionFit: A thema is a theme or subject, the central idea of a discussion or composition.

clue.text: They're (excessively?) liberal, last to be worried about boundary set back

indicators.note: set back means placed the other way round
one part goes round the other
letters that are worried are tugged about until they shift order

parts.note: taken as written, to be jumbled
in cricket a boundary clearing the rope without bouncing scores six

explanation.surface: Permissive types, the last people to fret about a boundary being pushed back.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a ball hit over the boundary scores six. LA(XIS)TS.
explanation.definitionFit: Laxists hold lax moral views, favouring the liberal side in cases of doubt, which critics consider over-lenient.

clue.text: Aussie bird displaying sexiness — I recount being entrapped by that

indicators.note: a thing entrapped by another is caught inside it

parts.note: SA is short for sex appeal
to recount is to tell

explanation.surface: An Australian bird flaunts its allure, and a witness describes being trapped by it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That' points back to the sexiness abbreviation, making it the container that traps the telling.
explanation.definitionFit: The sitella is a small Australian treecreeper-like bird, also called the varied sittella.

clue.text: Route artist's taken in varying tints

indicators.note: something taken in is absorbed into the middle of another
letters varying are altered in order

parts.note: taken as written, to be jumbled
RA, Royal Academician, is the standard abbreviation for artist

explanation.surface: A painter's path is worked into shifting colours.
explanation.walkthrough: T(RA)NSIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A transit is a passage or way across, a route by which people or goods are conveyed.

clue.text: One form of deception within another? That should help you get a grip

definitions.text: That should help you get a grip

indicators.note: one thing within another sits inside it

parts.note: another form of deception, a con trick
a ramp is old slang for a swindle

explanation.surface: A trick nested inside another trick ought to help you get a hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' does double duty: it signals the nesting and supplies the second trick. C(RAMP)ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A crampon is a spiked metal plate fixed to a boot for gripping ice when climbing.

clue.text: What spinner does, form of dismissal changing a test

parts.note: RO, run out, is a way a batsman is dismissed in cricket

indicators.note: letters changing swap places

parts.note: taken as written, to be jumbled

explanation.surface: A cricket picture: a spin bowler, a dismissal and a Test match.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a spinner is a slow bowler and run out is a dismissal, but the definition is literal: a spinning thing turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything that spins turns round on an axis, which is what the verb in the answer means.

clue.text: Finish making incision in part of face affected by rhinophyma?

indicators.note: an incision cuts into something, so this piece goes inside

parts.note: the nose is part of the face
to do is to finish, as in 'that's done'

explanation.surface: A surgeon completes an incision in a nose swollen by a skin condition.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhinophyma is a condition that makes the nose bulbous and lumpy, hence knobbly. NO(DO)SE.
explanation.definitionFit: Nodose means knotty or covered with knobs, an apt description of a nose swollen by rhinophyma.

clue.text: Ceanothus to procure through Amazon? Send it back

indicators.note: returning a parcel sends it back the way it came, so the phrase is read in reverse

parts.note: to order is how one procures goods from an online retailer

explanation.surface: Buy a garden shrub online, then return it.
explanation.walkthrough: TO ORDER read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Redroot is the North American name for New Jersey tea, a ceanothus shrub with a deep red root.

clue.text: Ponder this at large — it could create bane with torpedo?

definitions.text: Ponder this at large — it could create bane with torpedo?

indicators.note: letters at large are on the loose and free to rearrange

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; these letters are taken out

explanation.surface: Think of a vessel that could cause havoc with its torpedo.
explanation.walkthrough: Compositional: PONDER plus the answer rearranges into BANE TORPEDO, so take PONDER out and rearrange what is left. The whole clue also describes the boat.
explanation.definitionFit: An E-boat was a fast German torpedo boat of the Second World War, a menace to Allied shipping.

clue.text: Hill maybe getting e.g. Jack warm?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a first name, as of the comedian ... Hill, which is also Jack ... surname

definitions.note: noun: a warm coat, as in a British warm
definitions.meaning: second meaning: an overcoat, a warm being a British army overcoat

explanation.walkthrough: Benny Hill and Jack Benny were comedians, so 'Hill maybe getting e.g. Jack' turns the first name into a surname. 'Warm' is a noun: a British warm is an army greatcoat.
explanation.definitionFit: Benny is slang for an overcoat, and a warm is another word for a heavy coat.

clue.text: Contracts are horrifying with the writer behind time

indicators.note: one piece behind another follows it

parts.note: to appal is to horrify
T is the abbreviation for time
the writer refers to themself as I

explanation.surface: An author late with work finds the publishing contracts dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contracts' looks like a verb; it is the plural noun. APPAL + T + I.
explanation.definitionFit: Appalti is the Italian plural of appalto, a contract or monopoly, borrowed into English.

clue.text: Land in France and Germany once in equilibrium?

parts.note: pays is French for country or land
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A territory shared between France and Germany, balanced once upon a time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' marks an obsolete word: paysd is Spenser's spelling of peised, meaning weighed or balanced.
explanation.definitionFit: Paysd is a Spenserian past participle of peise, to weigh or poise, so it means balanced.

clue.text: Penny, old one being eclipsed by (relatively) new (7, two words)

indicators.note: something eclipsed is hidden behind or within another body

parts.note: recent means fairly new
d was the abbreviation for the old British penny, from Latin denarius

explanation.surface: The old penny is being displaced by newer coinage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old one' means an old penny, d in pre-decimal British money. RE(D)CENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A red cent is an American one-cent copper coin, the smallest sum, as in 'not worth a red cent'.

clue.text: Dark plain? That of Flanders was spoken ill of

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a dark lowland on the Moon's surface

definitions.text: That of Flanders was spoken ill of
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the insulting nickname given to Anne of Cleves

explanation.walkthrough: Henry VIII reputedly mocked his fourth wife, Anne of Cleves, as 'the Flanders Mare'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunar maria are dark basalt plains once thought to be seas, and a mare is also a female horse.

clue.text: Scotch presently had victory back up against English

indicators.note: one piece up against another sits right next to it

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English

indicators.note: a word going back is read from right to left

parts.note: to have won is to have had the victory

explanation.surface: A Scottish side that has won now finds itself up against England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotch' flags a Scots usage. E + NOW.
explanation.definitionFit: Enow is chiefly an old or dialect word for enough, but in Scots it also means just now or presently.

clue.text: With a good lather? Not so one's rolling in tub, the indirect way

indicators.note: the letters go inside the word for a bath

parts.note: a bath is a tub for washing

indicators.note: something rolling turns over, so its letters flip end to end
not having some letters means they are dropped

parts.note: soapy means covered in lather
taken as written; these letters are dropped
a means one; this letter is also dropped

explanation.surface: Not that lathered: someone wallowing in the bath takes the roundabout route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not so one's' removes two pieces, the word so and a letter meaning one, from the lather word; 'rolling' then flips what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A bypath is a side path or byway, figuratively the indirect way of getting somewhere.

clue.text: Slight cut during diabetic's medication

indicators.note: a word that is cut is shortened, losing its final letter

parts.note: a slight is an insult
in means during, as in 'in the night'

explanation.surface: A minor wound occurs while a diabetic is taking medication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slight cut' reads as a small wound; slight is the noun insult, and cut trims it. INSUL(t) + IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Insulin is the hormone injected by diabetics to control their blood sugar.

clue.text: Shrew, irritable and cross

parts.note: sore means annoyed, touchy
an X is a cross

explanation.surface: A shrewish woman is bad-tempered and cross.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shrew' reads as a scold, suiting 'irritable and cross'; it is the animal. SORE + X.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorex is the genus of common shrews, the small insect-eating mammals.

clue.text: High retro flat, needs changing inside

definitions.note: noun sense: a high, an elated state

indicators.note: retro means backward-looking, so the word is read backwards
the jumbled letters go inside the other word

parts.note: flat beer is stale

indicators.note: letters changing shift into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be jumbled

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned apartment needs redecorating within.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' looks like a home; it is stale. ELAT(EDNES)S.
explanation.definitionFit: Elatedness is a state of exhilaration, what someone feeling a high is experiencing.
